items.title: Most 'recurrent UTIs' in women aren't UTIs, study finds
items.summary: A study in The Journal of Sexual Medicine, reported by NPR, reviewed records of 253 women with recurrent UTI-like symptoms and found only 15% had infections confined to the bladder, while 85% showed hormonally driven vulvar inflammation and 75% had pelvic floor dysfunction. Lead researcher Dr. Maria Uloko says these conditions mimic UTI symptoms (burning, urgency, frequency) but need entirely different treatment than antibiotics.
items.sowhat: A myth-busting 'it's probably not a UTI' carousel positions Nancy as a brand that takes vulvar and pelvic health seriously, and opens a natural bridge into lubricant and pelvic-wellness content.
items.caption: Plot twist: that 'UTI' that keeps coming back might not be a UTI at all. Vulvar health is wonderfully complicated — bring curiosity, not just antibiotics 💛

items.title: New Kinsey/Playboy survey: the Gen Z 'sex recession' is real, but it's complicated
items.summary: The 2026 Playboy Gen Z Sex Survey, run with Julie and the Kinsey Institute among 2,373 US adults 18-29, found 29% had no sexual partners in the past three months and 19% have never had one. Top cited barriers were lack of opportunity to meet people (66.5%), fear of rejection (60%) and being 'too broke to date' (43%), even as desire for sex and romance stayed high.
items.sowhat: Reframe the 'sex recession' as a low-stakes, confidence-building opportunity rather than a problem, meeting anxious, cash-strapped Gen Z where they already are.
items.caption: Gen Z isn't 'less horny' — they're broke, busy, and terrified of being left on read. No judgment here: solo dates absolutely count 💫

items.title: Stanford study: heavy AI-companion use linked to lower well-being
items.summary: A Stanford study reported by CNBC surveyed 1,131 US adults and analyzed 464,687 messages from 237 Character.AI users, finding that people with smaller offline social circles leaned more on AI companions and reported greater loneliness and lower life satisfaction. Researchers concluded sustained AI companionship is associated with lower well-being, largely through reduced human interaction.
items.sowhat: A cheeky 'science says real hands beat chatbots' angle lets Nancy position its products as tools for actual human intimacy and confidence, not AI-companion substitutes.
items.caption: Science says: a chatbot can text you good morning, but it can't hold your hand. Real intimacy still wins 🤝

items.title: TikTok's new Community Guidelines crack down on sexually suggestive content
items.summary: TikTok published updated Community Guidelines and For You Feed Eligibility Standards, effective September 24, tightening enforcement against sexually suggestive behavior and significant adult body exposure. Such content is now age-restricted and ineligible for the For You feed, under a formalized three-tier enforcement ladder (warning, temporary restriction, account ban).
items.sowhat: Nancy's team should audit recent TikTok content for anything that reads as 'sexually suggestive' under the new standard and lean harder into humor/education framing to protect FYP reach.
items.caption: New TikTok rules just landed. If your FYP reach felt shy this week, that's why — we're keeping things classy (and still very visible) 👀

items.title: France drops its under-15 social media ban but keeps mandatory adult age checks
items.summary: After France's Constitutional Council struck down the original under-15 social media ban, Macron's government notified the European Commission of a revised law restricting about ten 'addictive' platform features for minors instead. The revised proposal still requires every adult user on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and X in France to verify their age, and Macron is pushing for it to become an EU-wide requirement.
items.sowhat: Nancy should start prepping age-verification-friendly account flows for French/EU followers now, since mandatory adult age checks are moving from 'maybe' to 'likely EU-wide.'
items.caption: Heads up, EU friends: proving you're an adult online is about to get very real in France. Wherever the rules land, we'll make sure you can still find us 🔐

items.title: Meta rewrites Health & Wellness ad rules to judge claims, not imagery
items.summary: Meta's updated Health & Wellness Advertising Standards shifted enforcement from a product-based approach to a claims-based one, so ads are now reviewed primarily on what they claim rather than what they depict. Sexual wellness products remain governed by this policy and must still target audiences 18+, with ads still barred from focusing on sexual pleasure or enhancement claims rather than health/medical efficacy.
items.sowhat: Still the operative standard for Nancy's paid Meta campaigns — copy should lean on wellness/health language over pleasure-forward claims to stay compliant.
items.caption: Meta's ad rules got a refresh: less before/after panic, same old rule about keeping things classy. We're adapting our ads to stay visible AND vibrant ✨
